Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Nature & food

world noun

the earth and its peoples

also the whole world, all over the world, worldwide, where in the world, globe, the globe, global, globally

classical

Liv. 1.16.7: caput orbis terrārum
Cic. Agr. 2.76: orbis terrae pulcherrimus (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 207
Traupman 205, 343, 408

orbis terrārum, orbis terrārum m.

noun, third declension, with a genitive

the world, the whole earth

Also orbis terrae, and in poetry orbis alone. “The finest in the world”: Cicero calls the land of Campania orbis terrae pulcherrimus.

Other words

  • mundus, mundī m. — the universe; the world of men

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. ND 2.154 (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 28.4: patria mea tōtus hic mundus est; Traupman 207, 408; Traupman 207

    Classically the ordered universe, the heavens, Greek κόσμος; in poetry and in Christian Latin the world and the people in it (Vulg. Jo. 8.12, ego sum lūx mundī).

  • ubi gentium? — where in the world?

    phrase: ubi with a genitive · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 465–470: ubi tū es gentium?; Traupman 172, 408: ubi terrārum?

    Not for the world, by no means: minimē gentium (Ter. Ad. 342).

Examples

  • caelestēs ita velle ut mea Rōma caput orbis terrārum sit

    (tell the Romans) that the gods wish my Rome to be the capital of the worldLiv. 1.16.7

  • ille terrārum mihi praeter omnīs angulus rīdet

    that corner of the world smiles on me more than any otherHor. C. 2.6.13–14

  • ubīque terrārum

    all over the worldTraupman 270

  • ubinam gentium sumus?

    where in the world are we?Traupman 408

  • pessimus poēta omnium

    the worst poet in the worldTraupman 408
